title: Machine Learning and Decision Support in Critical Care

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Machine Learning and Decision Support in Critical Care》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Clinical data management systems typically provide caregiver teams with useful information, derived from large, sometimes highly heterogeneous, data sources that are often changing dynamically.

evidence.text: Clinical data management systems typically provide caregiver teams with useful information, derived from large, sometimes highly heterogeneous, data sources that are often changing dynamically.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Machine Learning and Decision Support in Critical Care》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】Over the last decade there has been a significant surge in interest in using these data sources, from simply re-using the standard clinical databases for event prediction or decision support, to including dynamic and patient-specific information into clinical monitoring and prediction problems.

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】A range of applications addressing these issues are covered, including the modernization of static acuity scoring; on-line patient tracking; personalized prediction and risk assessment; artifact detection; state estimation; and incorporation of multimodal data sources such as genomic and free text data.

evidence.text: Over the last decade there has been a significant surge in interest in using these data sources, from simply re-using the standard clinical databases for event prediction or decision support, to including dynamic and patient-specific information into clinical monitoring and prediction problems.

A range of applications addressing these issues are covered, including the modernization of static acuity scoring; on-line patient tracking; personalized prediction and risk assessment; artifact detection; state estimation; and incorporation of multimodal data sources such as genomic and free text data.
